narrative:
Seven specialists produced fifty-eight surviving signals, but the audit shows they were not seven independent reads. Four source-pools were re-cut seven ways, and where three domains agreed they were usually reading the same document: one Technavio report in four vintages, one WNBA press release laundered three ways, one 2019 NBA PR estimate of 300 million players, one Nike PDP cited on both sides of the same gap. So the first job of a convergence lens is subtractive: strip the duplicate-as-corroboration, then see what still stands with independent evidence pointing the same way.

What survives that test is not what the domain opportunities assumed. Five genuinely independent evidence pools exist here: audited company and league disclosure; peer-reviewed physiology, biomechanics and primary rulebooks (A06-S1, A06-S2, A06-S3); verified event and participation operations (A05-S6, A05-S7, A02-S9); live product catalogue observation; and thin consumer-review corpora. Real convergence is where three or more of those pools point the same way about the same garment.

The strongest such convergence is structural, not a feature. The rules layer says competition shorts must clear the knee, carry no pockets and colour-match compression at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6). The biomechanics layer says fit must be validated in a lateral defensive stance, not standing (A06-S1). The consumer layer says the pocket is simultaneously the headline feature and the resented one (A01-S3, A06-S4). The commercial layer says the uniform channel is a separate, bookings-led, low-markdown pool (A04-S9). Four independent pools converge on one conclusion no single specialist stated: this is two products with one graded block, and the line is currently sold as one product to both. That is P-CONVERGENCE-1, and it reframes almost everything downstream.

The second convergence is uncomfortable. Nike's apparel grows on price and mix, not units (A03-S9); its volume short clears at 25 percent off with a 67 percent recommend rate (A04-S6); the reproducible defect is seams and shrinkage, not pockets (A01-S3); teen apparel mindshare is 26 percent against 46 percent in footwear (A01-S1); and four domains failed to find a SKU Nike ships with UV, a phone-secure zip pocket and a durability claim (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8). Independently sourced, these say the same thing: Nike's basketball shorts problem is discovery, make quality and merchandising, not invention. The most valuable candidates in this portfolio are therefore unglamorous.

The third convergence is women's, and it must be rebuilt rather than repeated. Strip the WNBA release and what remains is independent: Unrivaled's verified event economics (A05-S7), Australia's registry-grade female participation (A02-S9), a retailer CEO's first-party call quote naming cross-gender demand (A04-S5), and a live product read showing Nike already ships the assortment the files call empty (A03-S6, A07-S6). The demand is real and sustained; the whitespace is a length-and-rise system, not a category.

Two contradictions must travel forward unaveraged: inseam direction (A02-S5 against A07-S4) and China as growth versus contraction (A01-S7 against A02-S2, A02-S3, A04-S2). And one honest caveat governs every candidate below: no shorts-level unit, price or sell-through data exists in this base in any geography, so nothing here should carry a price recommendation.

patterns.title: Rules, biomechanics, consumer complaint and channel economics all say this is two products, not one
patterns.description: Four independent evidence pools converge on a line-architecture conclusion no single domain stated. Primary rulebooks require competition shorts to end above the knee, carry no pockets and colour-match compression worn at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6). Peer-reviewed biomechanics says fit must be validated in a lateral defensive stance and at jump-landing hip flexion, where hem and waistband bind (A06-S1). Consumer and product evidence says storage is the headline feature of the free-play short and simultaneously its most resented element (A01-S3, A06-S4, A07-S8, A03-S7). Commercial evidence says the competition garment is bought in a separate bookings-led, low-markdown B2B channel with different economics from the mall (A04-S9), while the free-play garment is bought at wholesale into a promotional floor (A04-S4, A02-S7). These are not the same source restated - rulebooks, a systematic review, review corpora and a dealer channel P&L have nothing in common. The conclusion is that the single 'basketball short' merchandised to both worlds is the root structural error, and that one graded block serving two explicitly different families is the cheapest correction.

patterns.title: The problem is capture, not invention: four domains could not find products Nike already ships
patterns.description: Independent of each other, A03, A06 and A07 each concluded that outdoor function, secure storage and UPF were unowned white space; the audit verified that one live SKU (Nike DNA 6" UV Woven) carries UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-secure zip pocket and an abrasion claim, closing all three at once. That single failure is one un-run query, not three findings - but the surrounding evidence for a capture problem is genuinely multi-pool and independent. Nike apparel grows on price and mix with units up only 1 percent (A03-S9). The volume franchise sits at 3.9 stars with 67 percent recommending on a real sample and the step-up franchise clears at roughly 25 percent off (A04-S6). Nike Direct has declined for ten consecutive quarters while wholesale grew (A02-S7). Teen apparel mindshare trails footwear mindshare by twenty points and is still falling among girls (A01-S1). Greater China apparel units fell 8 percent against growing participation, which A04 itself calls a capture failure rather than a demand failure (A04-S2). Five unrelated sources - a 10-K, a retailer review corpus, a channel disclosure, a teen survey and a regional unit read - point at the same conclusion: the assortment is not being found, trusted or converted.

patterns.title: Women's demand survives deduplication on four independent sources; the 'empty category' premise does not
patterns.description: The WNBA 2024 press release is one document that arrived through three domains and must count once. What remains after that subtraction is genuinely independent and still converges. Unrivaled's operations verify directly: ticket revenue up 204 percent, tickets sold up 249 percent, a professional women's record crowd, and a single Philadelphia night generating roughly one million dollars in tickets and four hundred thousand in merchandise (A05-S7). Australia's national participation registry - unconnected to any US league - shows female participation up 25 percent since 2022 past 450,000 (A02-S9). A retailer CEO says on his own earnings call that basketball is coming back built around women's basketball and that boys and girls are both buying it (A04-S5). A US teen survey shows Nike's female mindshare still declining (A01-S1). Four unrelated instruments, one direction. But the same pattern kills the product premise the domains attached to it: live catalogue evidence shows Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, WNBA fanwear and Sabrina bottoms, and put its most advanced cooling platform on a women's signature short first (A03-S6, A07-S6). The convergent whitespace is therefore a length, rise and coverage SYSTEM on a women's block, not an absent category.

patterns.title: Heat is the only functional need corroborated by physiology, institutional behaviour change and a competitor's multi-year platform
patterns.description: Three genuinely unrelated pools point at thermal load in outdoor basketball. Peer-reviewed measurement gives the only garment-level number in the entire base: basketball uniforms trap between zero and 1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity and with a wider range than treadmill running (A06-S2). Institutional behaviour change documents the consequence independently in the Philippines - meets moved away from 9am-3pm since 2024, and one 2024 provincial meet recording more heat-related than sports-related injuries (A06-S5). Competitor commitment corroborates commercially: Li-Ning's Wade UPF 50+ / AT Dry platform runs across consistent style codes from Spring 2023 through 2025, which is a sustained platform rather than a seasonal item, at a price far below Nike's (A03-S7). And Nike's own innovation direction independently agrees - cooling is its declared apparel vector, now shipped into basketball (A03-S4, A07-S2), with UV exposure and multi-hour tournament loads flagged separately (A06-S7). No two of these share a source. What none of them establishes is price, or that Nike's existing polyester does not already deliver the UPF claim.

patterns.title: Attention is inverted against evidence: the best-evidenced markets carry no opportunities and the worst-evidenced carries most of them
patterns.description: Ranking the surviving base by evidence quality rather than by strategic priority inverts the portfolio. Australia is the best-verified non-US market in the file - 1.3 million players, second among team sports nationally, female participation up 25 percent, NBL attendance above 1.2 million for a third consecutive season, and an on-court league partner that is not a performance-basketball leader (A02-S9) - and it supports one signal and no dedicated opportunity. Greater China carries the largest share of the portfolio on evidence that is geographically displaced at source (European and US resellers, a JD aggregator, a 2019 league PR estimate) while the measurable business contracts on every axis: Nike GC revenue down 13 percent currency-neutral with apparel units down 8 percent (A02-S2, A04-S2), Li-Ning basketball retail sales down 19 percent amid discounting (A02-S3), and e-commerce leadership flipped (A04-S11). Europe, Nike's second geography, is the primary market of exactly zero signals and appears only as a CAGR line (A02-S1). Live basketball is verifiably growing on every continent (A05-S6) but the absolute scale differs by an order of magnitude between markets. This is a portfolio-weighting pattern, not a product pattern, and it should govern where any Worldball candidate lands first.

patterns.title: The short is a top layer in a system, and three domains observed the system without naming it
patterns.description: Independently, the athlete, product and culture domains each described a garment worn over something else. FIBA's own interpretation makes compression undershorts legal at any length provided the team matches colour, which makes a layered system explicitly rules-safe (A06-S3, A06-S6). Biomechanics explains why the interface matters: activity changes every two to four seconds with roughly 450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps, so a waistband that slides on slick compression fabric is a repeated failure, not an occasional one (A06-S1). Women's sizing guidance orders by hip and leaves the waist under-controlled, dependent on a drawstring that slips when saturated (A06-S9, A06-S2). A regional market convention already ships the answer commercially - Philippine team practice pairs a compression liner with a loose short (A03-S10). And the coverage-first need is met by short-over-legging rather than by a longer short alone (A05-S8). Five observations, four domains, one unnamed product: a short engineered as a top layer with a defined interface to the layer beneath. Prevalence at the target sub-elite population is unmeasured, which is what keeps this moderate rather than strong.

patterns.title: Event-driven apparel demand is proven by a competitor in an adjacent sport and by verified live basketball operations, and used by no one
patterns.description: The mechanism and the occasion sit in different domains and have never been connected. Commercially, adidas grew apparel 35 percent in a quarter on World Cup demand in the same period its basketball fell 21 percent (A04-S3) - proof that event-anchored apparel lift is real and large, from a competitor's own disclosure. Culturally and operationally, live basketball is independently verified as growing and institutionalising: NBL attendance above 1.2 million for a third straight season (A02-S9, A05-S6), BAL attendance and video growth, streetball moved into stadium venues, and Unrivaled showing in-person demand and single-event merchandise revenue decoupling from broadcast (A05-S7). Channel evidence says the resulting product must be sold through wholesale and in-arena rather than as app-exclusive drops, because Nike Direct has fallen for ten quarters while wholesale grew (A02-S7, A02-S5). Three unrelated documents - a competitor's earnings commentary in another sport, league attendance releases, and Nike's own 10-K - point at a repeatable format nobody proposed. The calibration caveat travels with it: BAL's entire record season drew roughly nine NBL games' worth of people, so events must be sized to attendance, not to narrative.

candidates.name: Two Books, One Block
candidates.thesis: Split the basketball shorts line into an explicitly rules-governed Competition family and an unregulated Free-Play family built on one shared graded block, so that storage, hem and liner decisions stop being compromises made against two incompatible users.
candidates.intersection: Athlete/rules and biomechanics x Commercial channel economics x Consumer complaint evidence x Product and design line architecture
candidates.target_consumer: Two explicitly separated users on one block: (a) rostered competition players - US high school, AAU/club, college and FIBA-governed teams worldwide, boys and girls, bought through team dealers and specialty; (b) free-play and outdoor players 16-35 in the US, Greater China, Southeast Asia and Australia who arrive at a court by transit with a phone and no locker.
candidates.why_nike: Nike is the only brand with both a global team-dealer route to competition rosters and the DTC/wholesale reach for the free-play consumer, and it already owns a graded block, a compression business and the rulebook relationships. The correction is architectural rather than inventive, so it can be executed inside the existing cost structure - which matters when apparel growth is price-and-mix led with units up only 1 percent (A03-S9) and prices below USD 100 have limited headroom (A04-S8).
candidates.why_hard_to_see: The four inputs live with four different owners. The rules interpretation sits in team-sports compliance; the biomechanics sits in sports research; the pocket complaint sits in DTC review and returns data; the low-markdown bookings economics sit in a B2B P&L nobody in mall merchandising reads. A single PLM sees one 'basketball shorts' line and one blended margin, so the two users average into a compromise garment. It took six domains disagreeing about pockets and hems to reveal that they were describing two different products.
candidates.risks: Inseam direction is genuinely unresolved and this candidate does not settle it - A02-S5 and A07-S4 point in opposite directions, and Nike's live ladder runs 6-11 inches continuously with the longest length at the lowest price, which argues the 'commodity middle' is an active part of the business. Doubling families risks SKU proliferation into a promotional marketplace (A04-S4) exactly when Nike is working through inventory. The team-dealer growth case rests on a signal containing no basketball-shorts data of any kind (A04-S9), and core youth participation is contradicted rather than confirmed (A02-S1).

candidates.name: Layer-Ready Court Short
candidates.thesis: A linerless, knee-clearing competition short engineered as a top layer over compression - with a defined non-slip waistband interface, colour-matched to the tight - turning the one rules fact and the one physiology dataset nobody built on into a system Nike alone can sell complete.
candidates.intersection: Athlete/biomechanics and FIBA rule interpretation x Product/regional market convention x Culture/coverage need x Commercial team channel
candidates.target_consumer: High school, club/AAU, college and semi-pro players of both genders who already layer compression under game shorts; plus the coverage-first player - taller women, post players and modest-dressing athletes - for whom short-over-legging is the preferred solution rather than a longer short.
candidates.why_nike: Only Nike sells both halves of the system at scale and can colour-match them across a team order through the dealer channel, which is precisely the rules requirement (team must match colour). FIBA's own interpretation permits compression undershorts at any length, and the 2025-26 NFHS rule now permits teammates to wear multiple styles of like-coloured bottoms - so a Nike system can be sold as explicitly compliant while competitors sell a garment. The sewn-in liner it removes is a cost item, not an added one.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: Compression tights and shorts are different franchises with different PLMs, different fabric platforms and different margin structures, so nobody owns the interface between them. The enabling rule text is in an officials' interpretation document, not a trend report. And the strongest commercial precedent - the Philippine convention of pairing a compression liner with a loose short - is invisible from a US line-planning desk and appears in this base only as a footnote inside a price signal.
candidates.risks: Prevalence is the fatal unknown: the only quantitative compression survey is 88 percent endurance athletes, and layering rates among high school, club and college players are entirely unmeasured, so the linerless premise may serve a minority (A06-S6). Removing the liner is a downside-risk change for every player who does not layer, and there is no fit or returns data to bound it. The women's coverage evidence is stale (2014-2017 sources) even though the enabling rule change is current (A05-S8). Hot-market players in humid outdoor conditions may reject a second layer entirely (A06-S5).

candidates.name: Women's Length and Rise System
candidates.thesis: Not a new women's short but a women's block offered as a system - multiple inseams, a rise option, symmetric secure pockets and an adjustable waist - sold against a rule change that now explicitly permits teammates to wear different styles of like-coloured bottoms.
candidates.intersection: Athlete/fit and rules x Commercial/retailer demand x Culture/coverage and event demand x Product and design catalogue reality
candidates.target_consumer: Women and girls 14-30 playing school, club, college and pickup basketball - explicitly including the taller, post-playing and coverage-first minority currently served by nothing between a 5-6 inch default and a men's 11 inch - plus the WNBA/Unrivaled fan who buys game-day bottoms, in the US and Australia first.
candidates.why_nike: Nike already ships the SKUs (ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, WNBA fanwear) and has proven a USD 65 women's willingness-to-pay on women-specific construction, and it put Aero-FIT on a women's signature short before the rest of basketball - so the capability and the credibility exist. What is missing is a system: a single women's block expressed at multiple lengths and rises with pockets on both sides, which converts a set of unrelated styles into a franchise. That is a merchandising and grading investment, not an innovation bet.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: Every domain that looked at this described it as an empty category, and a live catalogue count shows it is not - so a PLM checking the claim finds it false and drops the whole thing, throwing out the real finding with the false one. The genuine opening is only visible when the fit data (hip-first sizing leaves the waist under-controlled), the rule change (NFHS multiple like-coloured styles), the coverage need and the actual SKU list are read together. Three of those four sit outside product entirely, and the rule change sits in an officials' manual.
candidates.risks: The 'under-assorted' claim is not evidenced - the WNBA growth numbers are two years stale and mis-transcribed, and Nike's live women's assortment is substantial (A03-S6, A07-S6). The fit thesis rests on Nike's generic women's-bottoms boilerplate, not on basketball-specific fit data, and the specialist itself found no quantitative women's fit-complaint corpus (A06-S9). Demand for a longer women's length is contradicted by retailer claims that long girls' shorts do not sell. Multiple lengths multiply size-curve risk in a promotional marketplace. And fan demand for jerseys is being read as player demand for shorts (A05-S1).

candidates.name: Outdoor Court, Found Not Invented
candidates.thesis: Nike already ships a short with UV protection, a phone-secure zip pocket and an abrasion claim, and four domains could not find it - so the outdoor opportunity is to name, spec-prove and merchandise an Outdoor Court family from existing capability rather than to invent one.
candidates.intersection: Product catalogue reality x Athlete/heat and UV physiology x Commercial/Greater China capture failure x Design system language
candidates.target_consumer: Outdoor and half-court players 16-35 on concrete, asphalt and acrylic in hot-humid markets - Greater China lower-tier cities, the Philippines, Southeast Asia, the US Sun Belt and Australia - who carry a phone and keys on-body and currently default to domestic value brands.
candidates.why_nike: The engineering already exists inside Nike; the failure is that it is invisible. Nike also has direct precedent for building China-specific outdoor product (the S.T. Flare, with an extra-durable outsole and reinforced high-wear zones distinct from US releases), so the organisational pattern is proven at footwear and simply not applied to bottoms. Turning existing SKUs into a named family with published spec proof - a UPF rating, an abrasion cycle count, a measured dry time - costs a fraction of a new platform and defends full price against domestic brands that already publish those claims.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: This is the single clearest artefact of the convergence lens: A03, A06 and A07 each independently concluded that outdoor function, secure storage and UPF were unowned white space, and all three were wrong for the same reason - each reasoned from the absence of a term in its own search to the absence of a product in the market. No individual PLM would see this either, because the SKU is real but is merchandised nowhere near the outdoor conversation and appears in no China outdoor assortment. It takes four domains failing identically to reveal that the gap is internal discovery, not external whitespace.
candidates.risks: The market is contracting where the opportunity is aimed: Nike Greater China revenue down 13 percent currency-neutral with apparel units down 8 percent, Li-Ning basketball retail sales down 19 percent amid deep discounting, and e-commerce leadership lost. The route to market is narrowing as Nike's largest GC retail partner exits online. Price is unanchorable - no Chinese price observation exists anywhere in this base, and Nike's own China outdoor precedent launched premium at RMB 899 while the value logic argues RMB 199-299. Peer-reviewed testing suggests 100 percent polyester already rates UPF 40-50 untreated, so a UPF claim may describe what the fabric already does rather than a new benefit.

candidates.name: Trapped-Sweat Spec
candidates.thesis: Specify the hot-market short against the one garment-level physiology number in the entire evidence base - the 0 to 1.33 kg of sweat a basketball uniform actually traps - turning 'breathable' from a marketing adjective into a published, testable claim that Nike's cooling platform can be measured against.
candidates.intersection: Athlete/peer-reviewed physiology x Athlete/institutional heat behaviour x Product/Nike innovation platform x Product/competitor platform commitment
candidates.target_consumer: Hot-humid-climate players - Philippine collegiate and barangay-league, Greater China outdoor, Southeast Asian and Gulf tournament players - plus competition players at the intensity tail everywhere, who play 40-60 minute runs in 27-32C.
candidates.why_nike: Nike has the only cooling platform in basketball apparel that has actually shipped (Aero-FIT reached basketball in July 2026 on a signature jersey and short), and it has the testing capability to publish a garment-level number that competitors claiming UPF and quick-dry do not publish. A measurable spec is also the only defensible answer to the audit's finding that Nike's premium rungs are discounted: an ASP-accretive feature needs proof, and this is the cheapest available proof because the protocol already exists in the literature.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: The number sits in a 2017 sports-medicine paper measuring sweat trapped in basketball uniforms - not a document any PLM, designer or trend analyst reads, and one that even the athlete specialist cited without using. The domain that found it built its recommendation on whole-body sweat rate instead, which is a physiology metric, not a garment metric. Only reading the physiology, the Philippine institutional evidence, the competitor platform and Nike's own tech roadmap together makes it obvious that everyone is arguing about cooling with no shared unit of measurement.
candidates.risks: A design decision is being presented as a finding: normative basketball sweat rate is 0.95 L/h - level with soccer and well below American football - so basketball is not a high-sweat sport by cross-sport standards, and engineering the line to the competitive tail carries different fabric, weight and cost implications than engineering to the sport mean (A06-S2). Every sweat measurement in the base is indoor, North American and overwhelmingly male, and is being used to justify hot-humid outdoor Asian and Gulf product. Aero-FIT's scaling economics and price are unverified, and Aerogami has not extended beyond one jacket in three years, which reads as a feasibility signal rather than white space (A07-S2).

candidates.name: Make-Quality Reset on the Volume Franchise
candidates.thesis: The highest-certainty margin and brand-trust return in this portfolio is not a new short but fixing seam construction and post-wash dimensional stability on the franchise that carries the units, because four unrelated evidence streams say the volume short is losing full-price productivity on make, not on design.
candidates.intersection: Consumer review corpus x Commercial markdown and margin x Product financial composition x Marketplace price-floor dynamics
candidates.target_consumer: Men and boys 16-35 buying core Nike basketball shorts at Dick's, Foot Locker, Walmart, Kohl's and JD in North America and EMEA - the largest single unit pool in the category and the one Nike already owns.
candidates.why_nike: This is Nike's own installed base, its own defect, and its own data. The evidence sample that matters was found by a skeptic, not a specialist: 3.9 stars with 67 percent recommending across 64 reviews at Dick's is a genuinely weak recommend rate on a real sample, and the reproducible complaints are seams failing and shrinkage after a single wash - a make problem, not a pocket problem as three domains assumed. Fixing it defends ASP that is currently mix-derived and already being eroded by discounts, and it requires no new platform, no new consumer and no new channel.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: The four inputs are owned by four functions that do not meet: review sentiment sits with consumer experience, markdown depth with sales, fabric GSM history with materials, and the composition of ASP growth with finance. Each on its own looks like noise - a bad review, a seasonal markdown, a mix effect. Read together they describe a franchise being cost-engineered into complaints while the marketplace trains consumers to wait for 25 percent off. It is also the least exciting candidate in the portfolio, which is exactly why no domain proposed it as its lead opportunity.
candidates.risks: The causal story is not established: nobody has shown that fabric weight actually changed, and the June 2025 sub-USD-100 price freeze that supposedly forced a cost-down has since been superseded by roughly 3 percent apparel price increases, so the margin-squeeze premise may be wrong (A04-S8). If GSM never moved, the recommended fix is expensive and aimed at the wrong defect. The sizing half of the complaint is base-rate neglect with no benchmark and no returns-reason data (A01-S2), and the pocket-failure claim could not be reproduced at all (A01-S3). A single end-of-summer markdown observation is not structural erosion (A02-S4).

candidates.name: Australia First, Not China First
candidates.thesis: Land the Worldball product in the market where the evidence is strongest rather than where the priority space points - Australia has registry-grade participation growth, a verified league, a non-performance on-court incumbent and Nike's existing doors, while every Greater China price and scale input in this base is displaced at source.
candidates.intersection: Marketplace/national participation registry x Culture/verified live-event operations x Commercial/competitive retreat and regional business reality
candidates.target_consumer: Australian players 14-30, disproportionately female and youth - 1.3 million participants, second among team sports nationally, female participation up 25 percent since 2022 past 450,000 - bought through Rebel, JD and Foot Locker Australia, with NBL fandom as the cultural surround.
candidates.why_nike: Nike is already distributed in these doors and faces a league on-court partner that is not a performance-basketball leader, against a competitive set that is retreating from performance basketball apparel globally. It is a proving ground with real participation, honest data, a settled route to market and no requirement to win a share war against domestic value brands in a contracting segment. Winning here produces a validated product and a real sell-through dataset - the exact thing this entire evidence base lacks - before the same block is taken into harder markets.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: Portfolio attention follows the stated priority space, and no individual specialist compares evidence QUALITY across geographies - each simply reports what its own searches returned. It takes counting the base by primary geography and by source provenance to see that roughly three quarters of it is US-derived, that the China narrative is assembled almost entirely from non-Chinese sources with no Chinese price observation anywhere, and that the single best-verified non-US market supports one signal and no opportunity at all. That is a structural bias in the research, invisible from inside any one domain.
candidates.risks: Australia is small in absolute terms and cannot carry a global line's volume; treating it as a proving ground rather than a market is the only defensible framing. Europe - the geography this candidate implicitly argues for next - has no signal where it is the primary market at all, so the case for it rests on audit-stage evidence rather than on the surviving base (A02-S1). Deprioritising Greater China runs directly against the stated SS28 priority space and against the largest participation claim in the base (A01-S7). The league on-court partner's status beyond the current term needs verification before any co-branded assumption.

candidates.name: Court-Day Capsule, Sized to Attendance
candidates.thesis: Build a repeatable shorts-first capsule format anchored to live basketball events and sized honestly to verified attendance, using the one competitor proof that event-driven apparel demand is real and large - and sell it through wholesale and in-arena, not through an app.
candidates.intersection: Commercial/competitor event-lift mechanism x Culture/verified live-event operations x Marketplace/channel reality
candidates.target_consumer: Event-going players and fans 16-30 at streetball and league moments - Melbourne and the NBL, Paris streetball, women's touring events - who buy a garment as a game-day identity object and wear it to play afterwards.
candidates.why_nike: Nike has the athlete roster, the graphic capability and the wholesale and in-arena reach to execute a repeatable format, and the mechanism is proven by a competitor's own disclosure in an adjacent sport - apparel up 35 percent in a quarter on tournament demand while its basketball business fell. A shorts-first rather than jersey-first format also addresses the genuine gap the culture domain identified without relying on the search data that failed audit: the fan wardrobe is being sold as tops while the lower body goes unserved.
candidates.why_hard_to_see: The mechanism evidence is in a competitor's earnings commentary about football; the occasion evidence is in league attendance releases; the channel constraint is in Nike's own 10-K. Nothing connects them inside a single domain, and the culture specialist that owned the occasion had no access to the commercial proof that the mechanism works. A PLM would also reasonably dismiss the occasion evidence on scale - until the competitor's number shows how large the lift can be when the event is large enough.
candidates.risks: Scale calibration is the binding constraint and cuts hard: the largest event in the base drew roughly nine NBL games' worth of people across an entire season, so most of these moments cannot carry meaningful volume. The resale and collab premise is hypothesis-only - every citation is a catalogue or product page with no price, premium-over-retail or sale-volume datapoint (A05-S10). At least one event's 2026 venue has changed from what the base assumes, so any drop planned against it is planned against stale information (A05-S6). Sport-as-fashion evidence is pan-sport and its strongest terms are for jerseys, not shorts, so the basketball-shorts inference is not supported by it (A05-S4). And the SS28 calendar itself - the events that would actually anchor this - appears nowhere in the surviving base.
